item.title: Lured by High Salaries, Some Brazilians Were Duped Into Fighting for Russia
item.description: Dozens of Brazilians were sent to the front lines with little training, and the high salaries they were promised, they say, turned out to be illusory.

item.title: After Cyberattacks and Bomb Threats Hit Europe, Survivalism Goes Mainstream
item.description: More governments in Europe are telling citizens to prepare for emergencies. After unexpected disruptions, many are listening.

item.title: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
item.description: The drop was largely driven by fewer people arriving from outside the European Union. It reflects government action to restrict immigration after a public backlash.

item.title: U.K. Releases Files on Peter Mandelson, Ambassador Tied to Jeffrey Epstein
item.description: Documents released Thursday shed new light on the rushed appointment of Peter Mandelson and his continued ties to Global Counsel, a lobbying group.

item.title: Police Link Release of Substance at Don Toliver Concert to Robbery Attempts
item.description: The police in Manchester, England, said they believed “organized criminals targeted people in the crowd to commit a series of robberies” during the concert on Sunday night.
